C1.statement: For every integer k >= 1 and every w in {0,...,9}^k, liminf as N tends to infinity of A_pi(w,N)/N is strictly positive.
C1.scope: The fixed nonterminating base-10 expansion of pi; all nonempty contiguous words including leading-zero words; overlapping starts 0 <= n < N.

T3.statement: For every k >= 1 there are H,N0 in N and epsilon,eta in R with N0 >= 1, epsilon >= 0, eta > 0, eta <= (1-H*epsilon-1/((H+1)*10^(-2k)))/(H+1), and for every N >= N0 and every nonzero integer h with |h| <= H, |sum_{j=0}^{N-1} exp(2*pi*i*h*fract(10^j*pi))| <= epsilon*N.
T3.scope: The fixed decimal pi orbit; one threshold N0 works for every later N and every signed frequency in the finite cutoff; witnesses may depend on k.
T3.formal_locator: finiteFourierLowerBound lines 33-37; eventual hypothesis lines 84-102; pi specialization lines 139-182

verdict_policy.YES: The cited result, with every premise source-verified, proves the exact target for fixed decimal pi.
verdict_policy.CONDITIONAL: A deterministic source-defined implication reaches the exact target after the stated unproved fixed-pi premise; there is no remaining base or quantifier mismatch after that premise.
verdict_policy.NO: The cited result has an indispensable scope, point, base, or conclusion mismatch. NO is only a corpus applicability verdict, not evidence that the target is false.

rows.locator: Hypothesis A and Theorem 1.1, retained author PDF pp. 2-3; explicit pi recurrence (3), retained PDF p. 3
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every integer b >= 2 and rational-polynomial perturbation satisfying the degree and nonsingularity assumptions, Hypothesis A conjectures finite attractor or equidistribution. Conditional on it, Theorem 1.1 makes fixed pi normal to base 2; the displayed pi recurrence has base 16.
rows.base: 16 for the pi recurrence, hence 2; not 10
rows.conditional_status: Explicitly conditional on unproved Hypothesis A.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: Hypothesis A is unproved; independently, even granting it the pi conclusion is base 16/2 rather than base 10.
C1.exact_comparison: Base-10 normality would imply C1, but no cross-base theorem in this result supplies decimal positive lower frequency.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: No conclusion concerns the orbit {10^j*pi}; the conditional orbit is {16^j*pi}.
T3.exact_comparison: No eventual bound is obtained for any decimal pi exponential sum, let alone one common N0 for all N >= N0 and 0 < |h| <= H.

rows.locator: Definition 2.1, retained author PDF p. 4; Theorem 2.2, retained PDF p. 5
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every real alpha and integer base b >= 2, alpha is normal to base b iff ({b^n alpha}: n >= 1) is equidistributed; normality means every length-k word has limiting frequency b^(-k).
rows.conditional_status: Unconditional equivalence, but neither side is established for fixed pi at b=10.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: Equidistribution of the fixed decimal orbit {10^n*pi}, equivalently base-10 normality of pi, is unproved.
C1.exact_comparison: The source conclusion would give A_pi(w,N)/N -> 10^(-k) for every k,w, which is stronger than C1.

T3.exact_comparison: Combined with the Weyl criterion, equidistribution gives normalized sum convergence for each h; finite intersection supplies a common N0 for a chosen finite H, and H,epsilon can be chosen so the displayed eta bound is positive.

rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: If alpha is normal to base b, then it is normal to every integer base c=b^r with nonzero rational r; the surrounding text warns that unrestricted transfer fails for bases not related by rational powers.
rows.base: base-transfer theorem; 16 and 10 are multiplicatively independent
rows.conditional_status: Unconditional transfer theorem whose premise and conclusion do not connect the available pi base to decimal.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: There is no nonzero rational r with 10=16^r.
C1.exact_comparison: Even a proof of base-16 normality of pi would not yield base-10 C1 by this theorem.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: The theorem supplies no transfer from the base-16 pi orbit to {10^j*pi}.
T3.exact_comparison: No decimal exponential-sum hypothesis is obtained.

rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every integer b >= 2 and theta in [0,1], digit-density is equivalent to density of the base-b remainder orbit, and base-b normality is equivalent to uniform distribution of that orbit.
rows.conditional_status: Unconditional equivalences; the fixed-pi decimal premise is not proved.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: Uniform distribution of the base-10 remainder orbit of pi is unproved.
C1.exact_comparison: Uniform distribution gives limiting frequency 10^(-k), hence C1; mere density/digit-density gives occurrence but not positive lower frequency.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: Uniform distribution of the fixed decimal pi orbit is unproved.
T3.exact_comparison: The same finite-frequency Weyl argument as row BC-ORBIT would give T3 for every k.

rows.locator: Strong Dichotomy Hypothesis and Theorem 4.1, preprint pp. 9-10 / journal pp. 361-362
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every BBP number to base b satisfying deg(q)>deg(p), the unproved Strong Dichotomy Hypothesis implies that the number is rational or normal to its BBP base.
rows.base: the known pi BBP base is 16, not 10
rows.conditional_status: Explicitly conditional on the Strong Dichotomy Hypothesis.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: The Strong Dichotomy Hypothesis is unproved; independently, the pi conclusion is in base 16 and does not transfer to base 10.
C1.exact_comparison: The theorem does not establish decimal block frequencies.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: No decimal BBP specialization for pi supplies uniform distribution of {10^j*pi}.
T3.exact_comparison: The theorem has no conclusion about the decimal sums in T3.

rows.locator: Section 1, equation (2) and Satz 1, printed pp. 313-315 (Satz 1 on p. 315)
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For an arbitrary real sequence alpha_n, uniform distribution implies vanishing normalized exponential sums for every nonzero integer m; Satz 1 proves the converse when sum_{h=1}^n exp(2*pi*i*m*alpha_h)=o(n) for every m != 0.
rows.conditional_status: Unconditional criterion, conditional application at the named point pi.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: The source does not prove the required o(N) sums for alpha_j=fract(10^j*pi).
C1.exact_comparison: If those sums held for every h, the orbit would be uniformly distributed and the orbit-normality rows would imply the stronger limit 10^(-k).

T3.first_unmatched_premise: For fixed pi, o(N) cancellation is unproved for every nonzero integer h.
T3.exact_comparison: For each k choose H with H+1>10^(2k), then epsilon small enough for a positive eta. Convergence at the finitely many |h|<=H gives one N0 valid for every N>=N0, exactly matching T3.

rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: A sequence x_n is uniformly distributed mod 1 iff for every nonzero integer h, (1/N) sum_{n=1}^N exp(2*pi*i*h*x_n) tends to zero.
rows.conditional_status: Unconditional iff criterion; no fixed-pi sum estimate is supplied.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: Normalized exponential-sum convergence for the fixed decimal pi orbit is unproved.
C1.exact_comparison: With that premise, uniform distribution and the decimal cylinder correspondence give limiting frequency 10^(-k), stronger than C1.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: The criterion supplies no proof of the fixed-pi convergence it tests.
T3.exact_comparison: Finite intersection over a chosen H converts the source's per-h limits into T3's common eventual N0; no effective threshold is required by T3.

rows.locator: Chapter 2, Section 2, Theorem 2.5 (Theorem of Erdos-Turan), equation (2.33), p. 112
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every finite real sequence x_1,...,x_N and every positive integer m, D_N <= 6/(m+1)+(4/pi) sum_{h=1}^m (1/h-1/(m+1))*|(1/N)sum_{n=1}^N exp(2*pi*i*h*x_n)|.
rows.base: base-neutral; specialize to the decimal pi orbit
rows.conditional_status: Finite deterministic inequality; supplies no pi-specific exponential-sum estimate.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: One still needs fixed-pi finite-frequency bounds making the right side eventually smaller than every fixed decimal-cylinder length with positive margin.
C1.exact_comparison: Such bounds would yield positive visits to every length-k cylinder; the theorem is a bridge, not a verification of those bounds.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: The inequality assumes the exponential sums as inputs and gives no upper bound for them at pi.
T3.exact_comparison: It does not prove T3's eventual sum hypothesis; rather, T3-type bounds can be substituted into it.

rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every fixed integer sequence n_j with n_(j+1)/n_j >= q>1, for Lebesgue-almost every x, the limsup of N*D_N({n_j*x})/sqrt(N*log log N) lies between the stated positive lower constant and C(q), with C(q)<=166+664/(sqrt(q)-1).
rows.base: set n_j=10^(j-1), so the lacunary base is exactly 10
rows.conditional_status: Metric theorem for almost every initial point, not a pointwise theorem.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: The source does not show that the named point x=pi lies in its conull set.
C1.exact_comparison: The theorem proves a strong positive-density/normality analogue for almost every x, but no fixed-pi conclusion.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: The almost-everywhere quantifier cannot be specialized to x=pi.
T3.exact_comparison: For almost every x the discrepancy scale would otherwise yield eventual finite-frequency cancellation, but this is not a fixed-pi proof.

rows.locator: Deterministic inequality (3.9) and note added, printed p. 250
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every finite real point sequence, |sum_{j<=N} exp(2*pi*i*x_j)| <= sqrt(32)*N*D_N; the note added improves sqrt(32) to 4.
rows.conditional_status: Deterministic at fixed pi, conditional on an unproved discrepancy estimate for that point sequence.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: No pinned theorem proves D_N({h*10^j*pi}) -> 0 for fixed pi at the needed frequencies.
C1.exact_comparison: A sufficiently strong fixed-pi discrepancy premise would imply the T3 sums and hence C1.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: A fixed-pi discrepancy bound tending to zero for each required h is unproved.
T3.exact_comparison: For chosen finite H, finitely many discrepancy onsets can be maximized to one N0; the inequality then gives |S_N(h,pi)|<=epsilon*N for every N>=N0.

rows.locator: Main Theorem and Corollary, manuscript pp. 1-2 / journal pp. 155-156
rows.exact_scope_quantifiers: For every fixed theta>1, for Lebesgue-almost every x, the normalized limsup discrepancies of {theta^k*x} equal Sigma_theta; for integer theta=10 the corollary gives the exact constant Sigma_10=sqrt(220)/27.
rows.conditional_status: Metric theorem for almost every x; no explicit exceptional set or named-point membership.

C1.first_unmatched_premise: The theorem does not establish its conclusion at x=pi.
C1.exact_comparison: Exact base-10 discrepancy for almost every x cannot be labeled as positive lower block density for fixed pi.

T3.first_unmatched_premise: The conull set is not known to contain pi (or h*pi/10 for the finite frequencies).
T3.exact_comparison: For an almost-everywhere analogue, finite intersection plus the deterministic Philipp inequality matches T3; it supplies no fixed-pi theorem.

bounded_conclusion: Within these six frozen sources and eleven rows, there is no YES verdict for C1 or T3 at fixed decimal pi. The criterion and deterministic rows identify conditional routes; the metric rows remain almost-everywhere only. This says nothing about sources outside the frozen corpus and is not evidence that C1 or T3 is false.
